meta.notes: Preliminary base built same-day ahead of a client meeting. Schema sampled directly (site has no Cloudflare-style bot block, unlike Stake); Ahrefs pulled live via API.

robotsIssue.title: Leaked template origins, held back only by robots.txt
robotsIssue.detail: The site's own robots.txt documents this directly, dated Sept 1 2026: these origin/template URLs return HTTP 200, are self-canonical, carry no meta robots tag, and render literal unrendered tokens like {{state}} and {{location_slug}} in the body. robots.txt is the only thing keeping them out of the index — blocking a crawl path doesn't remove a URL that's already indexed, and if the block is ever lifted before the template bug is fixed, Google will crawl and index broken pages at scale across every location.

genericBlogAttribution.note: 31 of the top 100 keywords by volume attribute to the generic /Blog index page instead of a specific article — not a real page ranking, a symptom of weak internal linking / canonicalization on those posts. Combined they represent 336,200 in monthly search volume.

schemaInventory.note: Best-built page type on the site — @id-linked org/location/service graph, medicalSpecialty, ReserveAction, priceRange
GAP: the single most important page for ‘testosterone replacement therapy’ has no Service, MedicalTherapy, or FAQPage markup — less schema than its own location subpages
Correct use of Physician type; see defect D1 on the name field
Generic BlogPosting regardless of medical content — no MedicalWebPage/reviewedBy
GAP: lists every clinic with zero ItemList/LocalBusiness markup for any of them

defects.title: Physician name field polluted with SEO title text
defects.description: Every sampled physician's schema.org Person.name is the full page-title string, not the person's actual name — confirmed identically on 2 of 2 sampled doctors.

examples.value: Dr. Alan Armstrong | Emergency Medicine Physician | Gameday Men’s Health
Dr. Robert Young | Emergency Medicine Physician | Gameday Men’s Health

defects.impact: Breaks Person entity disambiguation and Knowledge Panel eligibility for every doctor on the site — the correct value is the name alone, e.g. “Dr. Alan Armstrong.”

defects.title: postalCode field holds three different kinds of value
defects.description: The same schema.org field, across different nodes and locations, holds a real ZIP code, a city name, or a US-region name interchangeably.

examples.value: Abilene (a city name, not a postal code)
Southcentral Alaska (a region name, not a postal code)

defects.impact: Breaks structured geographic targeting for anything that actually parses postalCode as a postal code.

defects.title: Identical medicalSpecialty tags regardless of the physician
defects.description: Both sampled doctors — both titled ‘Emergency Medicine Physician’ — carry the exact same medicalSpecialty array (Endocrine, Urologic), suggesting a templated default rather than a per-physician value.
defects.impact: Same pattern seen on Stake: a sitewide template value standing in for what should be page/entity-specific data.

textVsDataGaps.evidence: 33 mentions of “FAQ” in the visible text of a single location/service page
textVsDataGaps.gapType: no FAQPage schema found on any sampled page

textVsDataGaps.evidence: 35 mentions of “testimonial” and 6 of “reviews” on the same page
textVsDataGaps.gapType: no Review or AggregateRating schema found anywhere sampled

textVsDataGaps.evidence: every LocalBusiness node has an address and a generic Google-Maps search link (hasMap)
textVsDataGaps.gapType: no GeoCoordinates (lat/long) on any sampled location, and no openingHoursSpecification

competitors.note: Blocked by bot protection — could not be scraped directly or via DataForSEO's crawler (403 on both). The biggest competitor is also the hardest to reverse-engineer.
Homepage only — zero JSON-LD found on their actual TRT service page (/mens/testosterone-replacement-therapy/). Gameday's location pages already carry more schema than this competitor's core page.
Smaller competitor, but has real FAQPage markup with Question/Answer pairs — exactly the gap Gameday has on far more FAQ content.

recommendations.title: Fix or remove the leaked template origins
recommendations.detail: robots.txt Disallow is not a fix — it only prevents new indexing. Either 404 the /regional-service/ and /clinic-service/ template paths or ship a real noindex, then let Google drop what's already blocked.

recommendations.title: Build out the pillar TRT service page
recommendations.detail: /service/testosterone-replacement-therapy should carry at least as much schema as its own location subpages — Service, MedicalTherapy, and FAQPage at minimum.

recommendations.title: Fix internal linking so blog posts stop folding into /Blog
recommendations.detail: 31 of the top 100 keywords by volume (336,200 combined monthly searches) currently attribute to the generic blog index instead of the specific article — the single highest-leverage fix available, larger than any schema change.

recommendations.title: Add FAQPage and Review/AggregateRating schema
recommendations.detail: Both exist as real content already (FAQ and testimonial sections) on location pages — zero-cost structured-data wins, same class of gap as Offer was for Stake.

recommendations.title: Fix the Person.name and postalCode defects
recommendations.detail: Both are template-level, one-time fixes that affect every physician and every one of the ~569 locations respectively.

recommendations.title: Add GeoCoordinates and openingHoursSpecification to every LocalBusiness node
recommendations.detail: Directly improves local-pack eligibility, which is already this site's best-performing channel (10 of its top local keywords rank in the top 5).
